q: A standard IPv4 ACL can filter traffic based on the destination TCP port.
why: Standard ACLs examine only the source address. Port-based filtering requires an extended ACL.

q: An ACL applied outbound on an interface does not filter traffic that the router itself generates.
why: Outbound ACLs inspect transit packets only, so router-originated traffic such as pings or routing updates from that router bypasses them.

q: With IEEE 802.1X, a device must authenticate, typically through RADIUS, before the switch port or wireless association gives it normal network access.
why: The supplicant authenticates through the authenticator to an authentication server; until it succeeds, only authentication traffic is allowed.

q: A GRE tunnel by itself encrypts the traffic it carries.
why: GRE only encapsulates. Pair it with IPsec (GRE over IPsec) to add confidentiality and integrity.

q: A WPA2-Personal passphrase is an ASCII string of 8 to 63 characters.
why: That is the allowed passphrase length for WPA2-PSK (a 64-hex-digit raw key is also possible). Longer, more random passphrases resist guessing better.

q: Dynamic ARP inspection relies on the DHCP snooping binding table to validate ARP packets.
why: DAI checks sender IP and MAC against snooping bindings (or static ARP ACLs) and drops ARP packets that do not match.

q: A computer worm needs a user to open an infected file before it can spread to other hosts.
why: Worms replicate across networks on their own by exploiting vulnerabilities. Needing a user action describes a virus or a trojan.

q: A script must add a new VLAN object through a controller's REST API. Which HTTP method represents the create operation?
why: In the CRUD mapping, create is POST, read is GET, update is PUT or PATCH, and delete is DELETE. GET only retrieves data and HEAD fetches headers without a body.

q: A REST client receives HTTP status 401 from a controller after several successful calls. What is the most likely cause?
opts: The request was processed and the resource was created
The token expired or was not sent
The requested resource does not exist on the controller
The controller experienced an internal software error
why: 401 means the caller is not authenticated, commonly an expired or missing token. A missing resource returns 404, an internal error is 500, and a successful creation is 201.

q: Given this JSON, what is the VLAN value of the interface that is not enabled? {"interfaces": [{"name": "Gi0/1", "enabled": true, "vlan": 10}, {"name": "Gi0/2", "enabled": false, "vlan": 20}]}
why: The interfaces key holds an array of two objects. The object with enabled set to false is Gi0/2, whose vlan value is 20. The value 10 belongs to Gi0/1, false is the enabled flag, and Gi0/2 is the name, not the VLAN.

q: In a controller-based architecture, which interface does a network management application use to request changes from the controller?
why: Applications talk to the controller through northbound APIs, usually REST. Southbound APIs run between the controller and network devices, and the data plane forwards user traffic rather than taking application requests.

q: A team wants to push configuration to routers over SSH using YAML playbooks and install nothing on the devices. Which tool fits?
why: Ansible is agentless, push-based and uses YAML playbooks. Puppet and Chef typically need an agent on the managed node and pull configuration from a server, and NetFlow is a traffic-reporting technology.

q: An engineer writes configuration files that describe the desired cloud network, then runs a plan to see what will change before applying. Which tool does this?
why: Terraform declares desired infrastructure state, compares it with recorded state, shows a plan and applies changes through providers. Ad hoc Ansible commands are imperative one-offs, SNMP is monitoring and CAPWAP is a wireless tunnel protocol.

q: Which statement best describes the key architectural change of software-defined networking?
opts: The data plane is moved off the switches and into a cloud service
Every device runs its own independent control plane for greater resilience
The control plane is centralised while devices keep forwarding
Management traffic is carried only in the data plane of each device
why: SDN separates the control plane from the data plane and centralises control decisions in a controller. The devices still forward, which rules out removing the data plane, and per-device independent control planes describe traditional networking.

q: In a fabric such as Cisco SD-Access, VXLAN tunnels carry user traffic between edge nodes across a routed network. Which part of the architecture do these tunnels form?
why: The overlay is the virtual network built with tunnels. The underlay is the physical routed network that gives the tunnel endpoints IP reachability, and APIs and the management plane are not forwarding constructs.

q: What is a primary advantage of managing a campus network with Catalyst Center (DNA Center) compared with configuring each device separately?
opts: It removes the need for any IP routing protocol in the campus
It replaces the physical links between switches with tunnels
It forces every device to run STP in every VLAN
Network-wide policy, templates and assurance from one place
why: A controller gives a single point to apply policy, automate provisioning and see assurance data for the whole network. It still relies on the underlay's routing and does not change physical connectivity or spanning tree.

q: A tool analyses months of WAN utilization data to warn that a link will be saturated in three weeks. Which type of AI capability is this?
why: Forecasting future conditions from historical data is predictive AI. Generative AI creates new content such as text or configuration, and a static threshold has no learning or forecasting.

q: A network assistant using generative AI proposes a configuration change for a production router. What is the best practice?
opts: Reject all AI output, since it cannot help with networking
Review and test the change first, since generated output can be wrong
Apply it immediately because AI output is always accurate
Apply it only to the access layer to limit risk without review
why: Generative AI can produce plausible but wrong configuration (hallucination), so human review, testing and change control still apply. Blind trust is unsafe, and rejecting all output wastes a useful assistant.

q: A configuration file holds three indented lines: "vlans:", then "- id: 10", then "name: Sales" under it. It has no braces, brackets or angle-bracket tags. Which data format is this?
why: Indentation with colons and dash-prefixed list items is YAML. JSON uses braces, brackets and quoted keys, XML uses nested tags, and CSV is comma-separated values.

q: Which two are benefits of network automation? (Choose two.)
opts: No more need for IP addressing
why: Automation reduces mistakes and keeps configuration uniform. It does not remove IP addressing or the data plane and it cannot guarantee zero downtime.

q: Which two statements describe REST APIs? (Choose two.)
opts: They run only over a serial console
They use HTTP methods such as GET and POST
The server stores a session for each client between requests
They are stateless, so each request carries what the server needs
why: REST is stateless and uses HTTP verbs on resources. Server-held sessions contradict statelessness, and REST responses are commonly JSON as well as XML.

q: Which two statements about Ansible are true? (Choose two.)
opts: It requires an agent on every managed node
It pulls configuration from managed nodes on a timer
why: Ansible is agentless and uses YAML playbooks pushed from a control node. Agents, pull models and Ruby-based definitions describe the Puppet and Chef family.

q: In a software-defined network, the data plane is moved from the devices into the controller.
why: The control plane is centralised; the devices still forward packets in the data plane.

q: An HTTP GET request is used to retrieve a resource without changing it.
why: GET maps to the read operation in CRUD; POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE change data.

q: In JSON, keys must be strings enclosed in double quotes.
why: JSON object keys are always double-quoted strings, and values can be strings, numbers, booleans, null, objects or arrays.

q: Generative AI output can be applied to production network devices without review because it is always correct.
why: Generative AI can produce confident but wrong answers, so changes still need human review, testing and change control.

q: Northbound APIs connect applications to a controller, while southbound APIs connect the controller to network devices.
why: North faces up to applications and administrators, south faces down to switches, routers and APs.
